fair_value_reason: Agent mean 9.07. Corrections on common inputs (9.0% WACC for non-contract flows, $5.0B net debt at Oct-27, 495M shares, overhead at the contract blend) plus method consistency: agent_1 10.69 -> ~9.40 (net debt -0.29/share; SOTP Barber Lake cap 6.5% -> 7.5% and overhead capitalized at the NOI multiple, SOTP 12.81 -> 9.94); agent_2 8.5 -> ~7.85 (WACC 8.5% -> 9.0%, net debt +$0.22B); agent_3 7.5 -> ~7.40 (net debt); agent_4 10.4 -> ~10.08 (net debt +0.57/share, overhead at contract blend -0.30, SOTP NOI $727M -> ~$707M and overhead 8x -> ~14x); agent_5 8.26 -> ~8.05 (WACC 8.0% -> 9.0%, net debt). Mean ~$8.56, about 45% below spot. Charging ~$35M/yr of future SBC to agents 2-5 would take ~$0.6 off.
supervisor_summary: Round 4 fixed site coverage: every agent now values all 14 inventory sites once, with the right MW, tenants, terms, payment direction and Colchis at 76%, no double-counted power and the sold JVs removed. Contract rates are soundly anchored on Cipher's own secured notes (AWS 6.5-6.75%, Fluidstack 7.25-7.75%, AI lab 7.75-8.5%). On common inputs the DCF is $6.32-9.55 split-rate (mean $7.42) vs $5.09-8.29 single-rate (mean $6.21). Overhead (and whether future SBC is charged), pipeline value and WACC now drive value more than the contract rate. Reconciled fair value is ~$8.6, about 45% below spot. I keep the mean ladder (P(>=15.46) 0.41) with low confidence and a $7.0 thesis break.
key_drivers: Contracted value is now well pinned down: site-level leases with split rates give contracted-only equity of ~$4.4-6.0/share. At $15.46, roughly two-thirds of the price rests on unsigned pipeline and multiple expansion.

Corporate overhead is now the single largest DCF swing: cash ~$115M/yr (10-Q). Whether future SBC (running ~$120M/yr in Q2-26) is charged is worth ~$1.1/share, and discounting it at WACC rather than the contract blend another ~$0.3-0.6.

Pipeline value ($0.85-1.73B, ~$1.7-3.5/share) rests on NPV per IT MW ($1.3-5.6M) and signing odds. Near-term catalysts are an Odessa, Reveille or Ulysses lease and ERCOT Batch Zero results (~Apr-2027).

Contract discount rates are anchored on Cipher's own secured notes (6.0-6.125% AWS, 7.125% Fluidstack). Splitting the rate adds only ~$0.7-1.6/share, because post-expiry, pipeline and overhead dominate the residual.
Rates (10-yr 5.12%, not 5.24%) and AI-infrastructure sector beta dominate the 12-month distribution.
